response:
I definitely prefer deep, focused conversations on a single topic most of the time. To me, the best parts of talking to someone are the nuances you only find when you stick with a subject—you get past the surface-level takes and start uncovering the messy, interesting contradictions, the personal connections that make a topic matter, or the little details that shift how you see the whole thing.

Jumping between subjects can be fun for a casual, low-stakes chat, but it often feels like we're just skimming the top of things without ever getting to the good stuff. I'd rather really dig into one idea thoroughly than bounce around and never move past "that's interesting." That said, I don't mind tangents if they feel organic—like if we're talking about a movie and veer into how the director's upbringing shaped their style, that's still part of the deep dive, not a random detour.
